newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese diplomat named leader of Sino-British body.
newsitem.headline: Chinese diplomat named leader of Sino-British body.

text.p: China has appointed a former official on Hong Kong affairs as its chief representative to a Sino-British diplomatic body hammering out details of the territory's transition to Chinese rule.

Wang Guisheng, a former director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office at Beijing's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, has taken up his new post at the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group, the semi-official China News Service news agency said on Wednesday.
Accompanied by his predecessor Zhao Jihua, 57-year-old Wang met his British counterpart Hugh Davies on Wednesday.

Wang has been closely involved with Hong Kong and Macau affairs in the past six years, having worked as counsellor, deputy director and director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, the agency said.
A professional diplomat for 35 years, Wang is proficient in English and Norwegian, having studied in Norway and worked at the Chinese Embassy in Oslo for a total of 21 years.
He is the fourth Chinese chief representative to the diplomatic group since its establishment in 1985.
China took Hong Kong back at midnight on June 30, ending 156 years of British colonial rule. Portugal is due to hand over its nearby island colony of Macau on December 20, 1999.
Zhao has been appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Hong Kong.
